questions.question: A peptide bond is formed between the:

options.A: Carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another
options.C: Side chains of two amino acids

questions.explanation: Condensation reaction with loss of water.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The alpha helix and beta pleated sheet are examples of:
questions.explanation: Stabilised by hydrogen bonds.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Adult haemoglobin (HbA) consists of:

options.C: Two alpha and two beta chains
options.D: Two alpha and two gamma chains

questions.explanation: HbF has two alpha and two gamma chains.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most abundant amino acid in collagen is:
questions.explanation: Every third residue is glycine; hydroxyproline stabilises the triple helix.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Sucrose is composed of:
questions.explanation: Lactose is glucose plus galactose.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The storage form of glucose in animals is:
questions.explanation: Stored mainly in the liver and muscle.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Phospholipids are important in the body as:
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are the main storage lipids.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In DNA, adenine pairs with:
questions.explanation: Guanine pairs with cytosine with three hydrogen bonds.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: mRNA carries the genetic code.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Transcription is the synthesis of:
questions.explanation: Translation produces protein from mRNA.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A codon consists of:

options.D: Three nucleotides specifying an amino acid

questions.explanation: Start codon AUG codes for methionine.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Kinases belong to which class of enzymes?
questions.explanation: They transfer phosphate groups from ATP.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The isoenzyme of creatine kinase specific for heart muscle is:
questions.explanation: CK-BB is in the brain; CK-MM in skeletal muscle.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An allosteric enzyme is regulated by:

options.A: Binding of a molecule at a site other than the active site
options.B: Competitive inhibition at the active site

questions.explanation: Shows sigmoidal kinetics.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: NAD+ is a coenzyme derived from:
questions.explanation: FAD is derived from riboflavin.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The main function of the pentose phosphate pathway is to produce:
questions.explanation: G6PD deficiency causes haemolysis on oxidative stress.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which hormone stimulates glycogen breakdown in the liver?
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glycogen synthesis.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Oxidative phosphorylation takes place in the:
questions.explanation: ATP synthase uses the proton gradient.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An uncoupler of oxidative phosphorylation (e.g. 2,4-dinitrophenol) causes:
questions.explanation: Brown fat uses thermogenin (UCP1).
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Lipoprotein lipase acts on:

options.C: Chylomicrons and VLDL to release fatty acids

questions.explanation: Located on capillary endothelium.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Fatty acid synthesis takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase is the key regulatory enzyme.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The major route of cholesterol excretion from the body is as:

options.C: Bile acids and bile cholesterol in faeces

questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Ammonia in the brain is detoxified mainly by conversion of glutamate to:
questions.explanation: Glutamine synthetase.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Alkaptonuria is due to deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Urine darkens on standing; ochronosis causes arthritis.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The end product of purine catabolism in humans is:
questions.explanation: Gout results from hyperuricaemia.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Creatinine is derived from:
questions.explanation: Serum creatinine reflects renal function.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The biological value of a protein is highest for:
questions.explanation: Milk protein is also of high value.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Vitamin A is needed for:

options.D: The visual cycle (rhodopsin) and epithelial integrity

questions.explanation: Deficiency causes night blindness.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Vitamin E is a:
questions.explanation: Protects membrane lipids from peroxidation.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Folic acid deficiency causes:

options.B: Megaloblastic anaemia and neural tube defects

questions.explanation: Methotrexate is an antifolate.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Raw egg white contains avidin, which causes deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Biotin is a cofactor for carboxylases.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Calcium absorption in the intestine is promoted by:
questions.explanation: PTH also increases calcium reabsorption.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which trace element is part of the thyroid hormones?
questions.explanation: Selenium is a cofactor for deiodinase.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Zinc deficiency is associated with:

options.B: Delayed wound healing, hypogonadism and acrodermatitis

questions.explanation: Zinc is a cofactor of many enzymes.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Basal metabolic rate is increased by:
questions.explanation: Normal BMR is about 1 kcal per kg per hour.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The normal fasting blood glucose is:
questions.explanation: Impaired fasting glucose: 100–125 mg/dL.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A rise in serum alkaline phosphatase is seen in:

options.B: Obstructive jaundice and bone disease (Paget's, rickets)

questions.explanation: Amylase is raised in pancreatitis.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A desirable total cholesterol level is below:
questions.explanation: LDL <100 mg/dL; HDL >40 mg/dL.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
